content: The document outlines a detailed system for recording and monitoring patients receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) for HIV care. It includes the following components: 1. ART Register Information: This section captures data such as the district and health facility where the patient is receiving care, the specific ART regimen (first-line, second-line, or third-line), the date ART was initiated, and the patient’s unique identification number. 2. Patient Demographics and Clinical Information: The register records the patient’s clinic ID, full name (surname and given name), sex, age, pregnancy status, breastfeeding status, and tuberculosis (TB) status. It also includes baseline CD4 count (or percentage for children under 5 years old), the date cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis was started, and any history of previous TB treatment. 3. Pregnancy Monitoring: For pregnant patients, the register tracks follow-up status, estimated delivery date (EDD), antenatal care (ANC) number, and HIV-exposed infant (HEI) number for each pregnancy. 4. Cohort Year and Month: The system organizes patients by cohort year and month of ART initiation, allowing for structured follow-up and monitoring. 5. Status at ART Start and Follow-Up: The patient’s clinical status at the time of ART initiation is recorded. Follow-up data is collected at regular intervals (e.g., months 0, 1, 2, 3, etc. If a patient discontinues ART (STOP), the reason for discontinuation and any interruptions (e.g., weeks off treatment before restarting) are documented. 6. Monitoring Outcomes: Sub-totals are calculated for follow-up outcomes, and reasons for treatment interruptions or discontinuation are noted. 7. Patients Not Starting ART Immediately: A separate list is maintained for patients who may not or will not begin ART soon after enrollment in HIV care. This includes the date of enrollment, unique ID, clinic number, name, sex, age, baseline CD4 count, and any history of previous TB treatment. This system is designed to align with consolidated guidelines for person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance, ensuring comprehensive tracking of treatment progress and outcomes.
